fields.explanation: Least-connections routing counts the requests still in flight on each server, so a server tied up by a 30-second job stops receiving new work until it drains. Round-robin and IP hash assign by position or client address, so they keep sending requests to a server that is already saturated, and a 20 ms request can end up queued behind a 30-second one.

fields.explanation: Caching pays when the same value is served many times before it changes, because every hit avoids the work and the staleness window stays short. Data that is unique to each request is never read twice, and write-heavy data is invalidated again before it is reused. Data that must be exactly current can still be cached only if every write updates the cache in the same operation, which moves the cost onto the writes.

options: Send every write to any replica and merge conflicts later

A replica cannot accept an independent write, and reading a write back from a replica can miss it while that replica is still catching up.

options: It should acknowledge each message before starting the work

fields.explanation: At-least-once delivery means a lost acknowledgment causes redelivery, so the handler can see the same message twice; an idempotency key, a dedup table, or a transactional write makes the second run harmless. Acknowledging before doing the work prevents the duplicate but turns a crash into a lost job, and in-process state does not survive the crash that caused the redelivery.
